clue.text: The fruit of playing harmonicas?

indicators.note: playing the instrument word is read as working its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about what comes out of blowing mouth organs.
explanation.definitionFit: A maraschino is a cherry preserved in the liqueur of the same name, so it is a type of fruit.

clue.text: Usual uproar after Spanish uncle decamps

indicators.note: decamps says the uncle leaves, so his letters come out of the uproar word

parts.note: an uproar is a commotion
tío is Spanish for uncle

explanation.surface: A family row breaks out once the uncle from Spain has stormed off.
explanation.definitionFit: Common and usual are synonyms for something ordinary or frequently met.

clue.text: Heartless student Yale finds a source of pain

indicators.note: heartless removes the insides of each of the two words, leaving only their end letters

explanation.surface: A cynical view that a cold-hearted Yale student is a pain in the neck.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is a painful inflamed swelling on the eyelid, so it is a source of soreness.

clue.text: Fail to block recording, admitting nothing more

indicators.note: to block means sitting in the way inside, so the failing word goes inside the recording

parts.note: a CD is a compact disc recording
to fail is to lose

explanation.surface: A complaint that a recording failed to stop, with no more entries allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: A door or list that is shut admits no further entrants, the sense of a venue that is full.

clue.text: Joyful quote picked up about cast in play

indicators.note: about means going around, so the reversed quote surrounds the other letters
in a down clue, picked up means lifted from bottom to top, so the quote word reads upwards

parts.note: to quote is to cite

indicators.note: in play means the letters of cast are rearranged

explanation.surface: A happy theatre story: a quotation gets noticed about the actors in a production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast in play' looks like theatre talk, but 'in play' just stirs the letters of cast.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstatic is a stronger synonym for joyful, meaning overwhelmed with delight.

clue.text: Fellow does badly with a heavy metal protection component

parts.note: someone who ails is faring badly in health
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron, a heavy metal

explanation.surface: A man struggles with a heavy metal part meant to keep things safe.
explanation.definitionFit: A fail-safe is a device that defaults to a safe state if something breaks, a protective component.

clue.text: Drink? Remain very empty

parts.note: to be is to remain in existence

indicators.note: empty strips out the middle of the word, keeping its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A drinker is told to stay, the glass being almost empty.
explanation.definitionFit: Bevy is British slang for an alcoholic drink, short for beverage.

clue.text: East German gripped by a force mostly related to preaching the gospel

indicators.note: gripped by means held inside, so the German word sits within the other letters
mostly means the last letter of the force word is dropped

parts.note: the police are a force
Ost is the German word for east

explanation.surface: A tale of an East German person held by the police, linked to evangelism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East German' is not a person: it is the German word for east.
explanation.definitionFit: Apostolic relates to the apostles, whose mission was to preach the gospel.

clue.text: Special speed in astronomical region

parts.note: pace is speed

explanation.surface: A particular velocity measured somewhere among the stars.
explanation.walkthrough: SP is also short for special, but ACE is not speed; S plus PACE works.
explanation.definitionFit: Space is the vast region beyond Earth's atmosphere studied by astronomers.

clue.text: He's on his dribble, finally exercising some fancy footwork?

indicators.note: exercising puts the letters through their paces, working them into a new order
finally takes the last letter of the word dribble

explanation.surface: A footballer on the dribble shows off clever moves with his feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Polishing footwear is work on what feet wear, so it is jokingly footwork of a fancy, shiny kind.

clue.text: Poor at planning, having very good line in confusion

parts.note: A1 or AI means first-rate, very good

indicators.note: in means the line letter is placed within the confusion word

parts.note: a mess is a state of confusion

explanation.surface: A disorganised person is excellent at one thing: drawing a line in a muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone aimless has no purpose or direction, which makes them poor at planning.

clue.text: Carriage still in reverse, about to turn

indicators.note: about means going around, so the reversed word surrounds the turning word
in reverse means the word for still is read backwards

parts.note: still means yet, as in 'still waiting'
to roll is to turn over and over

explanation.surface: A railway carriage is stationary in reverse gear, poised to swing around.
explanation.definitionFit: A trolley is a small wheeled cart or carriage for carrying goods or people.

clue.text: Study cable leading to a tense agreement

parts.note: to con is to study, an old sense
a cord is a thin cable
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A student pores over a cable, leading to a nervy deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A concordat is a formal agreement, especially between the Vatican and a state.

clue.text: Produces more garments the team declines?

definitions.text: Produces more garments the team declines?

parts.words: Produces more garments the team declines?
parts.note: split in two, the word suggests turning out more kits than a rival, or kits that a team rules out of use

explanation.surface: A kit maker turns out more shirts than the team ends up wanting.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb's everyday sense is to surpass; the clue plays on reading it as a prefix meaning 'more than' plus team kit.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstrip is to exceed, here wittily read as making more football kit, called strips in Britain, than others.

clue.text: Clothing size initially supplied by shops

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the word supplied

parts.note: a mall is a centre full of shops

explanation.surface: A clothing size is first stocked by retail outlets.
explanation.definitionFit: Small is a standard garment size, the one below medium.

clue.text: A lot of correspondence about each article in Die Welt prompts editorial

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shortened mail word goes round the other pieces
a lot of means most but not all, so the final letter of the mail word is dropped

parts.note: a letter is a piece of correspondence
der is a German definite article, as in the newspaper Die Welt

explanation.surface: A flood of readers' letters about a German newspaper prompts a leading article.
explanation.walkthrough: Die Welt is a German newspaper; its title supplies the idea of a German article.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaderette is a short leading article, that is, a brief editorial in a newspaper.

clue.text: Foolish response in marriage, a sudden movement belting one

indicators.note: belting means wrapping round like a belt, so these letters go round the one

parts.note: 'I do' is the response given in a marriage ceremony
I is the Roman numeral for one
a tic is a sudden involuntary movement

explanation.surface: A wedding vow followed by a sudden jerk that strikes someone looks silly.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiotic and foolish are synonyms describing stupid behaviour.

clue.text: I note some woodwind develops from related material

parts.note: NB, nota bene, means note well
reeds are woodwind instruments, or their vibrating parts

explanation.surface: A musician's observation about part of the woodwind section growing.
explanation.definitionFit: To inbreed is to produce offspring from closely related parents, so stock develops from related genetic material.

clue.text: Out to sea, drifting behind Commodore

indicators.note: behind means the drifting letters come after the officer's abbreviation

parts.note: Com. is the abbreviation for Commodore

indicators.note: drifting means the letters of 'to sea' wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A ship adrift out at sea, trailing the commodore's vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' looks part of 'Out to sea' but alone is the definition; 'drifting' makes ATOSE from TO SEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Out can mean unconscious, as in knocked out, which is a comatose state.

clue.text: Fancy that fellow will be captured by this French artist

indicators.note: captured by means held inside, so the man's pronoun goes within the French word

parts.note: ce is French for this
him refers to that fellow
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Imagine a man being caught by a French painter.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera is a wild fantasy or illusion, a sense of fancy as a noun.

clue.text: Men used teeth (part of skull)

parts.note: OR, other ranks, are the ordinary soldiers or men
bit is the past tense of bite, to use one's teeth

explanation.surface: Soldiers chewed on something, with a bracketed anatomical aside.
explanation.definitionFit: The orbit is the bony cavity in the skull holding the eye.

clue.text: Pope, agitated, left to be among simple marine folk

indicators.note: to be among means placed within, so these letters go inside the simple word

parts.note: mere means simple, nothing more than

indicators.note: agitated stirs up the letters of Pope into a new order

explanation.surface: An upset pontiff departs to live with plain seafaring people.
explanation.definitionFit: Merpeople are mermaids and mermen, mythical folk who live in the sea.

clue.text: Register I am surprised, having debts?

indicators.note: having means holding, so the debt word contains the exclamation

parts.note: being in the red means having debts
cor is a British exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Someone is startled to find they owe money and must sign up.
explanation.definitionFit: A register is an official list, and a record is the same kind of written log.

clue.text: Mercury perhaps showing level temperature

parts.note: a plane is a flat, level surface

explanation.surface: A thermometer's mercury showing a steady temperature reading.
explanation.walkthrough: Mercury looks like the liquid metal in a thermometer, but it is the world nearest the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercury is an example of a body orbiting the sun, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Early aviator down, avoiding onset of unfavourable storm

indicators.note: avoiding means the chosen letter is left out of the sad word

parts.note: to feel down is to feel blue

indicators.note: onset of takes the first letter of unfavourable

parts.note: a riot is a storm of disorder

explanation.surface: A pioneer flier comes down, steering clear of the start of a bad storm.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Blériot was the French pioneer pilot who first flew across the English Channel in 1909.

clue.text: Originated in border of Benin?

indicators.note: in places the little word between the two edge letters, the 'or' that links them as alternatives
the border of a word is its outer edge, its first and last letters

parts.note: the end letters of Benin are B at one edge or N at the other
the border of Benin is one end letter or the other, so the phrase also supplies the little word linking them as alternatives

explanation.surface: Someone was born on the edge of the West African country Benin.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: Benin's border is B at one edge or N at the other, so the conjunction OR sits in between.
explanation.definitionFit: Born means came into being, the sense of having originated somewhere.

clue.text: Place for student, American not English, to produce artwork

indicators.note: 'American not English' means A replaces E in the word

parts.note: a college is a place where students study

explanation.surface: A US student, rather than an English one, makes a piece of art at college.
explanation.definitionFit: A collage is a picture made by gluing scraps of paper and material, a type of artwork.

clue.text: Extended note in 22

indicators.note: in means the note letter goes inside the register word

parts.note: the answer to 22 down is a register, which is also a log

explanation.surface: A long musical note written into a record.
explanation.definitionFit: Long and extended are synonyms for something stretched out in time or length.

clue.text: Bumpy areas not good for journeys

indicators.note: not means the good letter is excluded from the bumpy word

parts.note: ridges are raised, bumpy strips of ground

explanation.surface: Travellers complain that rough terrain makes for unpleasant trips.
explanation.definitionFit: Rides are trips on a horse, bike or vehicle, so they are journeys.

clue.text: Tight rope finishing off chap

indicators.note: finishing off removes the final letter of the rope word

parts.note: a string is a thin rope
a gent is a chap

explanation.surface: A tightrope walker finishes off a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Stringent means strict or tightly controlled, as in tight rules.
